description: Flat turns a list of rows into one live list of cells
code:
rows = [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
cells = rows.flat()
assert(cells, [1, 2, 3, 4])
rows.push([5])
cells

description: A depth flattens that many levels and a depth of zero copies the list
code:
nested = [1, [2, [3, [4]]]]
two = nested.flat(2)
none = nested.flat(0)
assert(none, nested)
two

description: A class-level rule flattens each instance's own lists
code:
class Shelf(bins):
    this.bins = bins
$Shelf.items = $Shelf.bins.flat()
top = Shelf([["pen"], ["ink", "cap"]])
top.bins.push(["pad"])
top.items

description: Flattened grids answer aggregate queries as rows arrive
code:
grid = [[1, 0], [2, 1]]
cells = grid.flat()
total = cells.sum()
lit = cells.count(cell => cell > 0)
grid.push([3, 0])
[total, lit]

description: A depth converts as the index of at does
A null item that flattening reads settles the declaration to null
code:
gaps = [[1], null]
cells = gaps.flat()
kept = [[1, null]].flat()
[cells, kept]

description: A class population flattens to its instance list
code:
class Task
first = Task()
second = Task()
all = Task.flat(3)
third = Task()
all.length
